description: Raised from 10 on 2026-08-17. With ~26 dependencies moving per week and auto-merge on green, a limit of 10 protected nothing — it just hid work: 26 updates sat in the dashboard's Rate-Limited section, including the golang 1.26.6 and python 3.14.7 bumps that left ~87 code-scanning alerts open for weeks, and the ansible 14.3.1 bump whose absence broke develop's CI. 30 covers the weekly volume with headroom while still capping a runaway.

devcontainer.description: The stack templates and the examples open from a published image pinned to a release version tag plus that tag's index digest (<image>:vX.Y.Z@sha256:...); this manager moves the tag and the digest together. Renovate's default patterns only cover .devcontainer/devcontainer.json, which is generated from devcontainers/<stack>/ and disabled below; the companion workflow regenerates it.

packageRules.description: Do not try to pin GitHub Actions runner labels (ubuntu-latest etc.)
Auto-merge digest, pin, lockfile and non-major updates on green (develop is protected by CI Success)

Group the terraform-stack CLI tools, with the AWS CLI: it moved from the terraform Dockerfile to devcontainers/scripts/install-aws-cli.sh, the one pin devcontainer-terraform-aws and devcontainer-ansible-aws share, and stays in this group so its bumps keep arriving batched as before.

Hold CPython at 3.14 patches, in one group of its own. Renovate otherwise proposes 3.14.x to 3.15.x for the python docker dependency (the FROM python: lines, the podman base and ARG TOOLS_PYTHON_VERSION) and never a 3.14 patch, which is why CVE-2026-115557 needed a manual bump and why PR 565 stalled. 3.15 cannot build yet (uv pip compile for 3.15 fails: pyyaml 6.0.3 has no usable wheels), and TOOLS_PYTHON_VERSION in devcontainers/terraform/Dockerfile would join the terraform-stack group above, turning the whole group red and stopping terraform, terragrunt, tflint, sops, age, aws-cli and uv from auto-merging. Moving to 3.15 is a manual decision: widen allowedVersions then. This rule comes after the terraform group rule so its groupName wins (later rules win). matchDatasources keeps it off pyproject's requires-python. The regex accepts 3.14.10, 3.14.10-slim-trixie and 3.14-slim-trixie.

Group the AWS Python SDK: boto3/botocore/s3transfer ship as one lockstep release train, so separate PRs each rewrite uv.lock and the second one always lands in conflict (2026-07-24 and 2026-07-27, both times)

The Ansible collections the ansible images bake in (devcontainers/ansible/collections*.txt) move together: every bump rewrites the same file and Renovate Post-Process recomputes the artifact hashes on each PR, so one PR per batch instead of one per collection. Majors still get their own PR (separateMajorMinor).

One PR per release for the published images that the templates, the examples and the docs pin. A release adds the same version tag to every image, so the group moves every template together; without it each image gets its own PR and the stacks sit on different releases until the last one merges.

examples/ was ignored by config:recommended (ignorePaths above restates that preset without it) so that Renovate can move the image pins (version tag and digest) of the examples. Nothing else in examples/ is a dependency of this repository.

Generated files: Renovate must not edit them. requirements.txt and the requirements-*.txt exports come from uv.lock via `uv export`; .devcontainer/ is a copy of devcontainers/<stack>/ produced by scripts/use-devcontainer.sh. Editing generated files desynchronised the exports from the lock (2026-08-16, where it made a HIGH cryptography fix look applied while the lock stayed vulnerable) and duplicates every devcontainer PR: #411 patched .devcontainer while #412 patched the terraform template it is generated from. Renovate manages the sources; the companion regenerates the copies.

customManagers.description: uv version pinned as an ARG across the Dockerfiles

The CPython that uv installs for the pinned pre-commit and yamllint in the images not built on python:* (terraform, golang, latex), kept at the base image's version: same datasource and depName as the python:* FROM lines. A bump stays red until the pinned uv knows that Python build; bump uv first.
uv version in the ansible_environment role default
terraform CLI pinned as an ARG
terragrunt CLI pinned as an ARG
tflint CLI pinned as an ARG
sops CLI pinned as an ARG
aws-cli (git tags; both hashes recomputed by Renovate Post-Process). Pinned once, in the install script the terraform-aws and ansible-aws stages share.
tectonic (tag is tectonic@X.Y.Z; hash recomputed by a postUpgradeTask)

Ansible collections baked into the ansible images, one '<namespace.name> <version> <sha256>' line each (sha256 recomputed by Renovate Post-Process). Not the ansible-galaxy manager: it only reads requirements.yml-style files and marks any entry with a key besides name/version/source/type as unsupported, so a hash cannot sit next to the version there.

Versions pinned as *_VERSION env vars in workflows, tagged with a '# renovate:' annotation. Without this, pinning a tool version would freeze it forever — exactly how main ended up building from a base digest GHCR had already pruned (2026-07-24).

Version tag and digest of the published images that the documentation's dev container examples pin (<image>:vX.Y.Z@sha256:...), so that an example copied from the docs starts on the current release, as the templates do.

Version tag and digest of the Execution Environment image the podman profiles pin (<image>:vX.Y.Z@sha256:...). The devcontainer manager reads only the image and features properties, not a value in remoteEnv or customizations, and nothing else reads the smoke test, the execution-environment.yml template or the README. The image also has date tags (YYYYMMDD) and commit tags; docker versioning compares only tags of the same shape as the current one, so those never match a vX.Y.Z pin. The registry publishes the v<year>.<month>.<n> tags, so each January arrives as a major and waits for a person.

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: Security fixes must not wait for a human. The automerge rule below covers only patch/minor, so the cryptography 49->50 fix for a HIGH Bleichenbacher advisory sat open for six days purely because it was a major. CI still gates it: a red pipeline means no merge.
